2_Introduction: PSC with device efficiency (PCE) of 18.6495%, VOC of 1.1219 V, JSC of 24.666 mA/cm², and FF of 67.3952% was obtained. The core perovskite solution, composed of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 at 1.5 mol/L, served as the foundational matrix for the solar cell. For the fabrication of perovskite films, the perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. At 8 s before the end of the second step, 160 µL of CB was drop-coated to treat the perovskite films. The film was immediately annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation (Cs⁺ enhancing phase stability and suppressing halide segregation, FA⁺ providing optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor ~0.98 for α-phase retention, and Br⁻ partially substituting I⁻ to widen the bandgap while mitigating deep-level iodine vacancies)—undergoes highly sensitive crystallization kinetics governed by precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L), dual-speed spin-coating (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion), and precisely timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene at 8 s into the high-speed step), which collectively suppresses uncontrolled nucleation, minimizes PbI₂-rich intermediate phase persistence, and promotes uniform grain growth with reduced grain boundary density; this controlled solidification pathway—further stabilized by immediate thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min—lowers residual strain (evidenced by narrow XRD (110) peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6°), eliminates pinholes (confirmed by full-surface optical image coverage >99.2% and uniform grayscale intensity distribution across PL mapping), and yields homogeneous photoluminescence intensity with a monoexponential decay lifetime of 328 ns—signifying suppressed non-radiative recombination from bulk and interfacial defects; the resulting film exhibits minimal trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, as corroborated jointly by the high PL quantum yield, absence of spatially localized quenching in PL maps, and clean XRD phase signature—mechanistically enabling efficient charge extraction across both electron- and hole-transport interfaces, culminating in VOC of 1.1219 V, JSC of 24.666 mA/cm², FF of 67.3952%, and PCE of 18.6495%.
